MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  JULY 9, 2018
A regular meeting of the General Plan Advisory Committee (GPAC) of the City of Rolling Hills
Estates was called to order at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Committee Members Present:  Chair Zuckerman, Medawar, Addleman, Arata,
  Bayer, Buresh, Carman, Corman, Friedman,
  Shinn, Stegura,

  Committee Members Absent:  Schmitz, Carrese, Portugal, Seamans, Silvano,
  Wagreich

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Assistant City Manager
  Grammer, Sr. Planner Naughton, Administrative
  Assistant Corea

  Also present:  Mayor Huff

  Also present from Dyett & Bhatia:  Rajeev Bhatia, Meghan McNulty

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES,
  MEETING OF MAY 15, 2018

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR MADE A MOTION, SECONDED BY
  COMMITTEE MEMBER BURESH, TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE GPAC
  MEETING OF MAY 15, 2018, AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  Ellen Orenstein, Resident, expressed her concerns with the amount of traffic that the new
  development on Deep Valley Drive will bring. She also stated that there are not sufficient
  crosswalks on Deep Valley Drive and there are concerns with safety due to near accidents
  with vehicles and pedestrians.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  PROCESS UPDATE (DYETT & BHATIA)

  - Project status

  Rajeev Bhatia, Dyett & Bhatia, provided the committee with status on the task list and
  stated that the committee will continue to discuss future possibilities

  - Review of what we heard at GPAC Meeting #3

  Meghan McNulty, Dyett & Bhatia, provided a draft of the Draft Vision and Guiding
  Principles which were updated to include input provided from the last GPAC meeting. The
  draft document may be found on the City’s General Plan Update website page
  (https://rhegeneralplan.org).

  B.  GENERAL PLAN CONCEPTS BRAINSTORM (DYETT & BHATIA)

  Ms. McNulty stated that the objective for the meeting will focus on development ideas and
  opportunities on Silver Spur Road.

  - Review of current development projects

  1
GPAC Meeting Minutes
July 9, 2018
   Planning Director David Wahba provided a review of current development projects, which
  include:
  • Peninsula Pointe Assisted Living Project – currently in plan check and will
  be pulling permits in the near future. Background on this project was
  provided.
  • Merrill Gardens Project – this project has started and includes 114 assisted
  living units and 63 parking spaces.
  • New Parking Structure for the library and businesses from the former
  “Village” shopping center.
  • 927 Deep Valley Drive – this was approved in 2007 and is currently being
  built.
  • 627 Deep Valley Drive – under construction.

  Committee Member Corman asked about how to incorporate continuity between the
  various projects. Planning Director Wahba stated that this is something that the city has
  tried to do in the past and should be discussed for future developments.

  Committee Member Buresh asked about the proposed library annex. Committee Member
  Stegura stated that the library is raising money to put the annex on the roof level of the
  parking structure.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the original plan for Deep Valley Drive was to make
  the area pedestrian-friendly. The plan for “Little Silver Spur” was intended to also provide
  for a pedestrian experience.

  In response to an inquiry by CHAIR ZUCKERMAN, COMMITTEE MEMBER STEGURA
  stated that the library annex is used a lot and is the only teen after-school outlet on the
  Peninsula. When kids are in school, it is used by the seniors. The annex is also a
  significant revenue source for the library.

  In response to a question by MAYOR HUFF, Planning Director Wahba stated that there
  was discussion of the City’s vision to have a main community center. There are now
  several “centers” throughout the commercial district which includes the library. A comment
  was made that instead of a community center as a building, that developers that come in
  to the City create places that serve as places where the community can meet and gather.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there was an intention to do this at Peninsula Center.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the project at 927 Deep Valley Drive will include 75
  units with no age restrictions. He also stated that a mid-block crossing has been proposed.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the 627 Deep Valley Drive is approximately 80%
  complete and should open in the fall. This project includes 58 condominiums.

  Committee Member Shinn stated that with the increased number of vehicles the traffic
  control aspect is something that should be looked into. Committee Member Shinn
  expressed that the architecture is mixed up and suggested that pepper trees or another
  type of tree could tie it all together.

  - Silver Spur Road concepts brainstorm

  Mr. Bhatia asked Committee Members to state what they like about the Commercial
  District.

  •  Committee Member Friedman stated that she enjoys how close it is to her home
  and that it is easily accessible.
  •  Committee Member Arata stated that there are a lot of challenges with consistency,
  but he does walk there and enjoys that many services that he uses and places he
  shops are in close proximity.
  •  Committee Member Carman stated that it is centralized and has features that
  brings the community together.
  •  Committee Member Stegura stated that she likes the diversity of services and
  stores, but does not really visit the area too often.
  •  Committee Member Addleman expressed his concern with traffic.
  •  Chair Zuckerman stated that he likes that it is close and convenient and provides
  a wide variety of uses.
  •  Committee Member Buresh stated that she uses it a lot since her office is there
  and enjoys the variety of services.

  2
GPAC Meeting Minutes
July 9, 2018
   •  Committee Member Friedman stated that she walks from the Bay Club to CVS and
  uses the shops and services there.
  •  Committee Member Medawar stated that he has had his business there for 38
  years. There are challenges with the layout from one end to the other for
  pedestrians.

  A general discussion ensued on the challenges with the layout and accessibility concerns
  within the commercial district. In addition, the challenges with drawing customers to shop
  on the hill.

  Mr. Bhatia asked the Committee Members to state what they see as areas for
  improvement.

  •  Committee Member Addleman stated that the Promenade has been a failure and
  they tripled tenants’ rent and the Peninsula Center is doing quite well.
  •  Committee Member Stegura stated that with the increased number of vehicles that
  will be coming in to the city, will deter any efforts to reduce greenhouse gases.
  •  Committee Member Carman stated that there are challenges with the architecture
  and is not unified and does not give a sense of community. Committee Member
  Carman suggested having rental bikes in the area and stated that she does not
  believe adding more retail is what is needed, and added that people want places
  to go to feed their families and enjoy outdoor activities.
  •  Committee Member Shinn stated that uniformity throughout the district would help
  to make it more welcoming. Parking is also an issue and city cameras in more
  places for safety reasons. Committee Member Shinn stated that she would like to
  see more retail.
  •  Mayor Huff stated that efforts should be made to make improvements to what is
  existing in the City to make it a more attractive place to be.
  •  Committee Member Arata stated that there are a lot of good things in the city.
  He suggested widening sidewalks and planting trees to create a canopy which will
  also help to slow vehicles down. Committee Member Arata stated that the
  intersection at Silver Spur and Hawthorne could be improved to make it more
  attractive. In addition, creating ramps and ways to connect the various areas for
  pedestrians.
  •  Committee Member Corman stated that there are four different areas in the
  commercial district and there should be an effort to build on them individually but
  find a way to connect them.
  •  Committee Member Bayer expressed having a big box type store at the
  Promenade to draw people to shop there.
  •  Committee Member Friedman stated that she would like to see an open space for
  families to bring their children while they’re shopping.

  In response to a question by Mr. Bhatia, the Committee Members agreed that no additional
  housing developments should come in to the city.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the Brickwalk Project will be coming back and will
  include additional units. Residential has always been successful in the city.

  A discussion ensued regarding traffic into and out of the city and within the city. Mr. Bhatia
  stated that he will have their traffic engineering consultant review the traffic issues before
  putting together a plan to present to the committee.

  Mr. Bhatia asked the committee members to state what they would like to see at the
  Promenade.

  •  Chair Zuckerman suggested a small hotel, ancillary retail around a square and
  allow some residential units. A public space with opportunity for dining.
  •  Committee Member Medawar suggested reopening Deep Valley Drive. Relocate
  the Ice Chalet and add more restaurant and retail.
  •  Committee Member Shinn suggested housing with open space.
  •  Committee Member Stegura suggested a skate park or something for young
  people.

  Chair Zuckerman stated that an example the Riviera has independently owned businesses
  that are doing well. Committee Member Medawar stated that it is the small independently
  owned establishments that are thriving and the City has a good base for these types of
  establishments which are relationship based and driven when given a good spectrum of
  retail options.

  3
GPAC Meeting Minutes
July 9, 2018
   Committee Member Addleman suggested polling people on where they shop.

  Committee Member Shinn stated that younger people do tend to buy more expensive
  items and there will be a younger demographic moving into the city in the near future.

  Mr. Bhatia stated that the comments discussed at the meeting will be summarized and put
  together in a presentation and brought back to discuss at the next GPAC meeting.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS (Verbal Reports)

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting adjourned at 8:03 PM.

  __________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Minutes Secretary  City Clerk
